q: Quantum reverse Shannon theorem (Bennett-Harrow-Morgan-Smolin, Winter) states that a quantum channel N can be simulated using:
opts: Classical communication at rate C(N) (the classical capacity) and shared entanglement at rate E(N)
Quantum communication at rate Q(N) only
Forward classical communication at rate C_→(N)
exp: Quantum reverse Shannon theorem: any channel N can be simulated using E_{EA}(N) ebits of entanglement and C(N) classical bits, where E_{EA} is the entanglement-assisted classical capacity / 2. This is the 'reverse' of the classical Shannon theorem: any channel is as good as classical + entanglement of the same rates.
